title: Release Rollback
description: A fictional incident rehearsal: your team needs to decide whether to rollback a problematic production deployment or attempt an in-place fix.

cards.title: Alert: High Error Rate
cards.narrative: It's 3:00 AM. Monitoring shows error rate spike to 45% across all services. The last deployment (v2.3.1) deployed at 22:00. Error traces point to the new payment validation service.

cards.title: Rollback Decision
cards.narrative: You initiate rollback command. System begins restoring v2.3.0 from the last known good state. Rollback completes in 90 seconds.

evidence.label: Error Reduction
evidence.content: Error rate drops to 2% immediately after rollback

cards.title: Investigating Errors
cards.narrative: You open the error logs and see repeated connection timeouts to the database. The new validation service uses a connection pool size of 200, but the database max connections is 150.

evidence.label: Timeout Errors
evidence.content: 2,341 connection timeout errors in last 15 minutes

evidence.label: Database CPU
evidence.content: CPU at 98%, connections at max capacity

cards.title: Verification Complete
cards.narrative: All metrics normalized. Error rate at baseline, latency recovered. You schedule a post-mortem for tomorrow and update the incident status to resolved.

cards.title: Stakeholder Notification
cards.narrative: You draft a message to engineering leadership, customer success, and support team leads. You document the rollback decision, timeline, and root cause preliminary findings.

evidence.label: Root Cause (Preliminary)
evidence.content: Connection pool exhaustion in payment service

cards.title: Database Scaling
cards.narrative: You increase the database max connections to 300. The change requires a restart. While waiting for the restart, error rate continues to climb.

cards.title: Connection Pool Fix
cards.narrative: You deploy a hotfix reducing the connection pool to 100. The change deploys in 12 seconds. Error rate drops to 8% within 2 minutes.

cards.title: Database Restart
cards.narrative: The database restart begins. While waiting, you prepare rollback documentation and notify the on-call manager that the fix may take longer than expected.

cards.title: Restart Complete
cards.narrative: Database is back online with 300 max connections. Error rate drops to 3% over the next 5 minutes. The fix is stable.

cards.title: Monitoring Hotfix
cards.narrative: You watch the metrics for 15 minutes. Error rate stays at 2-3%. You prepare the incident report and schedule a follow-up review for the next day.

cards.title: Fix Applied
cards.narrative: You mark the incident resolved. The fix reduces connection pool size permanently. You create a follow-up ticket to add connection pool monitoring alert.
